title: Gram-scale synthesis of polyfluoroaryl sulfides via SNAr step
author: Chan, Lee, et al.
materials: A complete list of reagents and equipment can be found in the “key resources table”.

steps.title: Purify Triethylamine (optional)
steps.instruction: Pretreat 60 mL triethylamine with 1084.4 mg CaH₂ in a 100 mL oven‑dried single‑neck round‑bottom flask (6 mm × 24 mm Teflon stir‑bar), seal with a rubber septum, purge with nitrogen via a balloon and stir at room temperature for 14 h; then distill under nitrogen, heating slowly to 80 °C, collecting the distillate in three separate round‑bottom flasks while retaining 10–15 mL in the original flask. Quench the residual CaH₂ with methanol added to ice‑water in an ice bath and verify purity by ^1H‑NMR.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1084.4 mg CaH₂ into a 100 mL oven‑dried single‑neck round‑bottom flask equipped with a 6 mm × 24 mm Teflon stir‑bar.
Add 60 mL triethylamine.
Seal with a rubber septum and insert a nitrogen balloon through an inlet needle to maintain an inert atmosphere.
Stir at room temperature overnight (≈14 h).
Assemble a distillation apparatus under nitrogen, connect a cold‑water condenser, and wrap the condenser with cloth to prevent dripping.
Cover the distilling flask with aluminum foil for uniform heating.
Increase temperature slowly to 80 °C and collect the distillate in three separate round‑bottom flasks via a cow‑type receiver.
Leave 10–15 mL triethylamine in the original flask to avoid contact with residual CaH₂.
Quench the remaining CaH₂ by adding methanol dropwise to an ice‑water bath.
Analyze the distilled triethylamine by ^1H‑NMR to confirm the absence of impurities.

steps.title: Monitor Reaction Completion via TLC
steps.instruction: After the allotted reaction time, withdraw 0.2 mL of the reaction mixture, mix with 1 mL EtOAc and 1 mL saturated NH₄Cl(aq) in a 4 mL vial, shake 20 times, let stand 30 s, then spot the organic layer on a TLC plate alongside starting material and thiol; develop with hexane, visualize under 254 nm UV, and confirm disappearance of the perfluoroarene (Rf ≈ 0.8). Extend the reaction if starting material remains.

substeps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe, draw 0.2 mL of the reaction solution into a 4 mL vial containing 1 mL EtOAc and 1 mL saturated NH₄Cl(aq).
Close the vial, shake about 20 times, and let stand for 30 s.
Dip a capillary into the upper (organic) layer and spot onto a TLC plate together with samples of the perfluoroarene starting material and the thiol.
Develop the plate in a hexane mobile phase inside a sealed chamber.
Inspect the plate under a 254 nm UV lamp; the product spot should have Rf ≈ 0.8.
If the starting material spot is still visible, continue the reaction until it is fully consumed.

steps.title: Extract Reaction Mixture
steps.instruction: Transfer the reaction mixture to a 125 mL separatory funnel, add 20 mL saturated NH₄Cl(aq), shake until layers separate, then perform three successive extractions of the aqueous phase with 20 mL EtOAc each, combine all organic extracts, dry with 2 g anhydrous MgSO₄ (adding 1 g increments if needed), filter, and remove solvent by rotary evaporation (180 mbar, 40 °C, 30 min).

substeps.instruction: Rinse the reaction vial with 20 mL EtOAc and transfer the combined solution to a 125 mL separatory funnel.
Add 20 mL saturated NH₄Cl(aq) and shake until the organic and aqueous layers are clearly separated.
Collect the aqueous layer in a 100 mL beaker; repeat the addition of 20 mL saturated NH₄Cl(aq) and shaking two more times (total three extractions).
Transfer the organic layer(s) to a 100 mL beaker.
Add 20 mL EtOAc to the aqueous layer, shake, and combine this organic extract with the previous organic layers.
Add 2 g anhydrous MgSO₄ to the combined organic solution and stir with a glass rod until no suspended particles remain; if no suspension appears, add MgSO₄ in 1 g increments (avoid excess).
Filter the suspension through a Büchner funnel with 70 mm filter paper, washing the residue twice with 15 mL EtOAc each time.
Collect the filtrate in a 125 mL round‑bottom flask and evaporate the solvent on a rotary evaporator at 180 mbar, 40 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Load Sample onto Silica Gel
steps.instruction: Dissolve the crude residue in 30 mL dichloromethane, add 2 g silica gel, evaporate to dryness at 750 mbar, 40 °C for 15 min to obtain a silica‑bound crude, then slurry the silica with 100 mL hexane/10 mL EtOAc, and pack the mixture into a column, back‑filling solvent five times until the silica is tightly packed.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 mL dichloromethane and 2 g silica gel to the crude residue and stir to form a uniform slurry.
Remove the solvent on a rotary evaporator at 750 mbar, 40 °C for 15 min, yielding a dry silica‑bound mixture.
Prepare a slurry of 42 g additional silica gel in 100 mL hexane + 10 mL EtOAc.
Transfer the silica‑bound crude (from step 1) into the column and back‑fill with the slurry solvent five times under pressure until the silica bed is tightly packed.
Use a plastic funnel to add the silica gently, leaving about 0.5 cm of solvent above the silica surface.

steps.title: Perform Column Chromatography
steps.instruction: Overlay the packed silica column with a thin layer of sea sand, then elute with hexane/EtOAc (10:1) while collecting 11 mL fractions; monitor each fraction by TLC (as in step 2) to identify those containing the product.

substeps.instruction: Place a layer of sea sand on top of the packed silica bed to protect the surface.
Begin elution using a hexane : EtOAc mixture (10 : 1 v/v).
Collect eluate in 11 mL test tubes.
Analyze each fraction by TLC (spot, develop with hexane, visualize under 254 nm UV) to locate the target compound 2‑((perfluoropyridin‑4‑yl)thio)benzo[d]thiazole.
Pool all fractions that show the product spot.

steps.title: Isolate and Dry Final Product
steps.instruction: Combine the product‑containing fractions in a 250 mL round‑bottom flask, evaporate solvent on a rotary evaporator at 300 mbar, 40 °C for 30 min, then apply high vacuum for 15 min to afford the white solid (1084.0 mg, 0.3428 mmol, 85.7 % yield).

substeps.instruction: Transfer the pooled fractions into a 250 mL round‑bottom flask.
Remove solvents on a rotary evaporator at 300 mbar, 40 °C for 30 min.
Place the flask under high vacuum (≈0 mbar) for 15 min to eliminate residual solvent.
Collect the white solid product (1084.0 mg, 0.3428 mmol, 85.7 % isolated yield).

description: Aromatic thioethers are attractive targets for the development of new efficient synthesis protocols being a recurring motif in bioactive compounds,2,3 pharmaceuticals,4,5 and materials science.6,7 This predilection is further amplified with the limitations purported from reported literature methods such as poor regioselectivity and the necessity of transition metals.8,9 Other protocols for the synthesis of polyfluoroaryl sulfides are also rather complex; requiring hetarenium salts that act as an activated substrate for thiolation10,11 or are comported into focused settings such as in the preparation of polymers12 and in peptide stapling.13,14 We further reckoned that a straightforward, metal-free approach for the synthesis of polyfluoroaryl sulfides could provide a solution to the previously mentioned challenges. With SNAr as a viable pathway, a general protocol that is regioselective, cheap, and simple is disclosed to provide para-thiolated polyfluoroarenes in a wider substrate scope, lower overall cost, and good to excellent yields. Additionally, this protocol is amenable to late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives and is commutable to solvent-free mechanical ball milling15,16 and flow reaction,17 please refer to Liao et al.1 We have also previously applied this protocol for the installation of pentafluoropyridines in benzyl mercaptans and mercaptoacetates, which activates the latter two for the desulfurative nickel-catalyzed reductive Liebeskind−Srogl type cross-coupling with aryl halides.18
